notes.method: Per motion_diversity.ipynb (make_plot_ind + calc_stopping_point): at each step n, MMD(multiscale kernel) between S_n upsampled with a random resample of itself and S_{n+b}, b = 5% of n; 20 resamples (seed 0). mmd_std = 1 std over the 20 resamples (the notebook stores 2*std and uses that as the tolerance band). stopping_point: knee of the 5-pt-smoothed curve (kneed, S=5) then 5 consecutive steps inside the running band; -1 = never saturated. Main curve starts at 50 (paper, diversity.tex line 13); stopping_point_start100 uses init 100 as the notebook did.
notes.ordering_caveat: The saved embeddings are NOT in generation order: EvaluatorModelWrapper.get_motion_embeddings sorts by motion length (descending) and returns that order, so "the first n descriptions" in the notebook are the n LONGEST motions. generation_order (only for realworld/pamap2/usc-had) re-embeds the clips in prompt-index order with the same evaluator (verified to reproduce the saved vectors, median NN distance < 0.004 vs norm ~10.6).
notes.paper_claim: IMUGPT 2.0 diversity.tex line 47: most saturation points fall within ~400-600 descriptions. That claim is about the text-description saturation algorithm (text embeddings, not in the repo); this file is motion-embedding diversity.
notes.stochasticity: Stopping points depend on the random resampling: re-running the notebook on realworld_2000 with 3 seeds moved e.g. standing from 488 to 1161 and running from 620 to 651. Treat single values as indicative.
notes.notebook_check: Re-running this code on realworld_2000 with init 100 reproduced the notebook saved outputs closely: climb down 239/262 (nb 239), climb up 199-228 (nb 199), jumping 228-250 (nb 250), lying 228 (nb 239), sitting 228-239 (nb 228), standing 488 (nb 488), walking 262-288 (nb 262); running 620-651 vs nb 443 (nb used calc_steps(2000) on 2,024 rows).

saturation_points_used_in_paper.source: size of motion_embedding/t2m-gpt/myogym_1000_optimal/<act>.npy = number of descriptions kept by the saturation-point algorithm (init 100, +5%/step; which modality drove it, text or motion, is not recorded in the repo - the paper says text); these sets presumably underlie the With Saturation Point rows of tables/algo_eval.tex. Values are all on the calc_steps(.,0.05,100) grid.
